lines.japaneseText: その〇〇、すごく似合ってますね。
lines.englishMeaning: That ___ really suits you.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Ask where she found it, then let the topic move on naturally.
lines.notes: Replace 〇〇 with the actual item: clothing, an accessory, a hairstyle. The specificity is the whole point.

lines.japaneseText: すごくいい雰囲気ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You have a really nice vibe.
lines.notes: Works in social spaces where strangers already talk to each other.

lines.japaneseText: おしゃれですね。思わず声かけちゃいました。
lines.englishMeaning: You're stylish, so I ended up saying hello.
lines.notes: Says plainly why you approached, which is easier to answer than a line that hides its intent.

lines.japaneseText: なんか楽しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You look like you're having fun.

lines.japaneseText: なんか話しやすそうな雰囲気ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You seem easy to talk to.

lines.japaneseText: ちょっと緊張してますけど、話しかけてみました。
lines.englishMeaning: I'm a little nervous, but I wanted to say hello.
lines.notes: Honesty instead of performed confidence. Low pressure because it admits the awkwardness rather than papering over it.

lines.japaneseText: こんにちは。なんか気になったので、挨拶だけでもと思って。
lines.englishMeaning: Hi. You caught my attention, so I wanted to at least say hello.
lines.followUpSuggestion: If the answer is short, thank her and leave it there.
lines.notes: Frames the whole thing as a greeting, not a request, so there is nothing she has to decline.

lines.japaneseText: 一度話してみたい雰囲気だなと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: You seemed like someone I'd like to talk to.

lines.japaneseText: すごく自然に目に入りました。
lines.englishMeaning: You naturally caught my attention.

lines.japaneseText: 今日ここに来てよかったです。
lines.englishMeaning: I'm glad I came here today.
lines.notes: A warm mid-conversation remark rather than an opener.

lines.japaneseText: 今、目合いましたよね？笑
lines.englishMeaning: We just made eye contact, didn't we?
lines.notes: Only when it clearly happened more than once. Otherwise it sounds like an accusation.

lines.japaneseText: さっきから何回か目が合ってる気がします。
lines.englishMeaning: I think we've caught each other's eye a few times.

lines.japaneseText: 目が合ったので、挨拶しようかなと思って。
lines.englishMeaning: We caught each other's eye, so I thought I'd say hello.

lines.japaneseText: 笑ってくれたから、話しかけても大丈夫かなと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: You smiled, so I thought it might be all right to say hello.
lines.notes: Needs an actual smile directed at you, not a general good mood.

lines.japaneseText: その笑顔で、話しかける勇気が出ました。
lines.englishMeaning: Your smile gave me the courage to come over.

lines.japaneseText: さっき目が合ったとき、話しかけようか迷ってました。
lines.englishMeaning: When we caught each other's eye earlier, I was debating whether to say something.

lines.japaneseText: それ、美味しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That looks good.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Ask what it is, then order it yourself if the reply is warm.

lines.japaneseText: そのメニュー、僕も迷ってました。
lines.englishMeaning: I was torn over that item on the menu too.
lines.notes: Best while queueing or ordering nearby.

lines.japaneseText: ここ、雰囲気いいですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: This place has a nice atmosphere.
lines.notes: For shared counters or communal tables. A café is not automatically a social space.

lines.japaneseText: この店、初めてなんですけど当たりですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's my first time here, and it was a good call.

lines.japaneseText: その飲み物、見た目すごいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That drink looks spectacular.

lines.japaneseText: そのステッカー、〇〇ですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: That sticker is ___, isn't it?
lines.followUpSuggestion: Shared interest is the easiest thing in the world to keep talking about. Ask how she got into it.
lines.notes: Only if you actually recognise it. Guessing wrong is worse than saying nothing.

lines.japaneseText: 僕もそれ頼めばよかったです。
lines.englishMeaning: I should have ordered that.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、カフェ日和ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Perfect weather for sitting in a café.
lines.notes: For a terrace or patio on a good day.

lines.japaneseText: それ、何飲んでるんですか？美味しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: What are you drinking? It looks good.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Order the same thing, or ask what else they recommend here.

lines.japaneseText: 今日ここ、いい雰囲気ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Good atmosphere here tonight.

lines.japaneseText: ここ、初めてですけど当たりですね。
lines.englishMeaning: First time here, and it turned out well.

lines.japaneseText: そのお酒選ぶの、センスいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That's a good choice of drink.

lines.japaneseText: ここのおすすめ、詳しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You look like you know what's good here.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Let her recommend something and then actually order it.

lines.japaneseText: なんか一番話しやすそうだったので来ました。
lines.englishMeaning: You seemed like the easiest person here to talk to.

lines.japaneseText: まずは乾杯だけしてもいいですか？
lines.englishMeaning: Could we just have a toast first?
lines.notes: Needs both of you to already be holding a drink.

lines.japaneseText: 一人で飲んでる仲間を発見しました。
lines.englishMeaning: I've found a fellow solo drinker.

lines.japaneseText: ここ、一人でも入りやすくていいですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's nice that this place is easy to come to on your own.

lines.japaneseText: 今日は軽く一杯のつもりだったんですけど、楽しくなりそうです。
lines.englishMeaning: I only came for one drink, but this is turning into a good evening.

lines.japaneseText: その注文、常連感ありますね。
lines.englishMeaning: That order has real regular-customer energy.
lines.notes: Needs a genuinely specific, confident order.

lines.japaneseText: その乾杯に混ざりたいくらい楽しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You all look like you're having such a good time I want to join the toast.

lines.japaneseText: その笑い声につられて来ました。
lines.englishMeaning: Your laughter drew me over.

lines.japaneseText: その席、一番楽しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That looks like the best seat in the place.

lines.japaneseText: その曲、最高ですね！
lines.englishMeaning: This track is great!
lines.notes: Short by design. In a loud room a long sentence is just noise.

lines.japaneseText: めっちゃいいノリですね！
lines.englishMeaning: You've got great rhythm!

lines.japaneseText: 今日一番楽しんでますね！
lines.englishMeaning: You're having the best time here tonight!

lines.japaneseText: いい笑顔ですね！
lines.englishMeaning: Great smile!

lines.japaneseText: 一瞬だけ乾杯しません？
lines.englishMeaning: Quick toast?

lines.japaneseText: 僕より全然踊れてますね！
lines.englishMeaning: You dance far better than I do!
lines.notes: Self-deprecating, which keeps it light.

lines.japaneseText: 今日来て正解でしたね！
lines.englishMeaning: Coming out tonight was the right call!

lines.japaneseText: 名前だけ聞いてもいいですか？
lines.englishMeaning: Could I just get your name?
lines.notes: Only once you are already talking and the noise makes anything longer impossible.

lines.japaneseText: すみません、そのコーデすごく素敵ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Excuse me, that outfit is really great.
lines.notes: Approach from the front or side, leave several feet of space, and stop the moment she keeps walking. Never follow.

lines.japaneseText: そのバッグ、すごくセンスいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That bag shows real taste.

lines.japaneseText: 髪色すごくきれいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your hair colour is beautiful.

lines.japaneseText: そのネイル、かなり凝ってますね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your nails are really intricate.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Ask whether she chose the design herself.

lines.japaneseText: そのキャラクター好きなんですか？僕も気になってました。
lines.englishMeaning: Do you like that character? I've been curious about it too.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、この辺すごく人多いですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's really crowded around here today.
lines.notes: The lowest-pressure opener there is. Costs nothing to ignore.

lines.japaneseText: そのお店、何か良さそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That shop looks promising.

lines.japaneseText: その傘、デザインかわいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your umbrella has a lovely design.

lines.japaneseText: すみません、急いでなければ一言だけ。すごくおしゃれだと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry, just one thing if you're not in a hurry. I thought you looked really stylish.
lines.notes: Builds her exit into the sentence, which is what makes a direct daytime approach reasonable.

lines.japaneseText: ナンパっぽく聞こえたら申し訳ないんですけど、すごく素敵ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry if this sounds like a pick-up line, but you look wonderful.
lines.notes: Use sparingly. Naming the awkwardness works once, not repeatedly.

lines.japaneseText: それ、美味しいですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: That one's good, isn't it.
lines.notes: Keep it to one exchange. Most people here are mid-errand.

lines.japaneseText: 僕もいつもそれ買います。
lines.englishMeaning: I always buy that too.

lines.japaneseText: その新商品、気になってました。
lines.englishMeaning: I've been curious about that new one.

lines.japaneseText: その組み合わせ、絶対美味しいやつですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That combination is definitely a good one.

lines.japaneseText: 僕も夕飯で完全に迷ってます。
lines.englishMeaning: I'm completely stuck on what to have for dinner too.

lines.japaneseText: その本、面白いですよ。
lines.englishMeaning: That book is good.
lines.notes: Only if you have actually read it.

lines.japaneseText: それ、僕も気になってました。
lines.englishMeaning: I've been curious about that too.
lines.notes: Best when you are both looking at the same thing.

lines.japaneseText: その作家、いいですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: That author is great.

lines.japaneseText: 同じ棚を見てるってことは、趣味が近いかもしれませんね。
lines.englishMeaning: If we're looking at the same shelf, maybe our tastes are similar.

lines.japaneseText: その作品好きなら、〇〇も合いそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: If you like that, ___ might suit you too.
lines.followUpSuggestion: A real recommendation gives an obvious reason to exchange contacts later.

lines.japaneseText: ここ来ると予定より長居しちゃいますね。
lines.englishMeaning: I always end up staying here longer than I planned.

lines.japaneseText: そのジャンル好きな人と話してみたかったんです。
lines.englishMeaning: I've been wanting to talk to someone who likes that genre.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、外にいるのが気持ちいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It feels good to be outside today.

lines.japaneseText: その犬、すごくかわいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your dog is lovely.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Talk to the dog first and let the conversation arrive on its own.
lines.notes: Ask before touching the dog.

lines.japaneseText: すごく人懐っこいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: He's very friendly.
lines.notes: For when the dog has come to you first.

lines.japaneseText: ここ、夕方の雰囲気いいですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: The atmosphere here in the evening is lovely.
lines.notes: Daylight and other people around only. Never approach someone sitting alone after dark in a quiet spot.

lines.japaneseText: その写真、いい感じに撮れそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That looks like it'll make a good photo.

lines.japaneseText: いい場所知ってますね。
lines.englishMeaning: You know the good spots.

lines.japaneseText: ここの夕日、毎回ちょっと得した気分になります。
lines.englishMeaning: This sunset makes me feel like I've got away with something every time.

lines.japaneseText: 浴衣、すごく似合ってますね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your yukata really suits you.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、雰囲気最高ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: The atmosphere today is wonderful.

lines.japaneseText: その食べ物、正解っぽいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That looks like the right choice.

lines.japaneseText: その景品、取れたんですか？すごいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Did you win that? That's impressive.

lines.japaneseText: 花火始まる前からもう楽しいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's already fun and the fireworks haven't even started.

lines.japaneseText: お祭りって、知らない人とも話しやすくなりますね。
lines.englishMeaning: Festivals make it easier to talk to people you don't know.

lines.japaneseText: その団扇かわいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That fan is lovely.

lines.japaneseText: 〇〇ですよね？完成度高いですね！
lines.englishMeaning: You're ___, right? The execution is superb!
lines.followUpSuggestion: Ask how long the build took. Cosplayers usually enjoy that question.
lines.notes: Naming the character correctly is the entire compliment.

lines.japaneseText: その衣装、細かいところまですごいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: The detail on that costume is remarkable.

lines.japaneseText: ウィッグのセット、めっちゃきれいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: The wig styling is beautifully done.

lines.japaneseText: 小物、自作ですか？すごく本物っぽいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Did you make the props yourself? They look completely real.

lines.japaneseText: その作品好きな人に会えて嬉しいです。
lines.englishMeaning: It's great to meet someone who likes that series.

lines.japaneseText: 写真お願いしたくなる完成度ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: The quality makes me want to ask for a photo.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Ask permission before photographing, and stop if the answer is no.

lines.japaneseText: 撮影終わったあと、少し作品の話したいです。
lines.englishMeaning: Once you're done shooting, I'd like to talk about the series a bit.
lines.notes: The right line when she is currently busy being photographed: it waits instead of interrupting.

lines.japaneseText: コスだけじゃなくて、本人の雰囲気にも合ってますね。
lines.englishMeaning: It suits not just the cosplay but you as well.
lines.notes: A more personal compliment. Only once you have actually been talking.

lines.japaneseText: この曲、生で聴くと全然違いますね。
lines.englishMeaning: This song is completely different live.
lines.notes: Between songs, never during one.

lines.japaneseText: さっきの曲、最高でしたね。
lines.englishMeaning: That last song was superb.

lines.japaneseText: そのバンド好きなのが伝わります。
lines.englishMeaning: It's obvious how much you love this band.

lines.japaneseText: そのTシャツ、かなりレアですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: That shirt is pretty rare, isn't it.

lines.japaneseText: 今日のセットリスト、強すぎますね。
lines.englishMeaning: Tonight's setlist is ridiculous.

lines.japaneseText: 耳大丈夫ですか？音かなり大きいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Are your ears all right? It's seriously loud.
lines.notes: Genuine concern, best on the way out or in a quieter corner.

lines.japaneseText: 今日の練習、かなりきつかったですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That session was hard going.
lines.notes: After class, never mid-set. Never comment on her body, weight, flexibility or clothing fit.

lines.japaneseText: あのコンビネーション、上手かったですね。
lines.englishMeaning: That combination was well done.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、先生いつもより厳しいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: The instructor is tougher than usual today.

lines.japaneseText: 僕、途中で完全にバテてました。
lines.englishMeaning: I was completely finished halfway through.

lines.japaneseText: 同じ曜日によく会いますね。
lines.englishMeaning: We seem to end up here on the same days.
lines.notes: Only when it is genuinely true and has happened naturally.

lines.japaneseText: そのグローブ、デザインいいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Those gloves have a great design.

lines.japaneseText: 練習仲間がいると続けやすいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's easier to keep at it with training partners.

lines.japaneseText: さっきの話、面白かったです。
lines.englishMeaning: What you said earlier was interesting.

lines.japaneseText: 説明がすごく分かりやすかったです。
lines.englishMeaning: Your explanation was really clear.

lines.japaneseText: 発音きれいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Your pronunciation is lovely.

lines.japaneseText: 僕も同じところで迷いました。
lines.englishMeaning: I got stuck in exactly the same place.

lines.japaneseText: 初参加同士っぽいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: We both look like first-timers.

lines.japaneseText: さっきから共通点が多い気がします。
lines.englishMeaning: I feel like we keep finding things in common.

lines.japaneseText: まだちゃんと話してなかったですね。
lines.englishMeaning: We haven't properly spoken yet.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、誰と知り合いなんですか？
lines.englishMeaning: So who do you know here?
lines.followUpSuggestion: The answer usually hands you the next three questions.

lines.japaneseText: まだ乾杯してなかったですね。
lines.englishMeaning: We haven't had a toast yet.

lines.japaneseText: 僕たち、共通の友達以外にも共通点ありそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: I suspect we have more in common than just the mutual friend.

lines.japaneseText: 結構並びますね。
lines.englishMeaning: Quite a queue, isn't it.
lines.notes: The safest opener in the library. Easy to answer, easy to ignore.

lines.japaneseText: ここまで並ぶと期待値上がりますね。
lines.englishMeaning: After queueing this long the expectations go up.

lines.japaneseText: 進んだと思ったら全然進んでないですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Just when you think it's moving, it isn't.

lines.japaneseText: その選択、人気みたいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Looks like that's the popular choice.

lines.japaneseText: 一人で並ぶより、ちょっと話せるほうが楽ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Queueing is easier with someone to talk to.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、電車かなり混んでますね。
lines.englishMeaning: The trains are really packed today.
lines.notes: Open, populated platform only. Never inside a near-empty carriage, never late at night, never where she cannot easily walk away.

lines.japaneseText: この路線、よく遅れますね。
lines.englishMeaning: This line is often delayed.

lines.japaneseText: そのキーホルダー、〇〇ですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: That keyring is ___, isn't it?

lines.japaneseText: 急にすみません。その服、すごく素敵だと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry to interrupt. I thought your outfit looked wonderful.
lines.notes: Daytime, busy platform. Do not ask where she lives or which stop she is getting off at.

lines.japaneseText: 急に降ってきましたね。
lines.englishMeaning: That rain came out of nowhere.

lines.japaneseText: この雨、聞いてないですよね。
lines.englishMeaning: Nobody warned us about this rain.

lines.japaneseText: 傘持ってる人が勝ち組ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Anyone with an umbrella is winning today.

lines.japaneseText: 今日、暑さが本気すぎますね。
lines.englishMeaning: The heat is not messing about today.

lines.japaneseText: 雨宿り仲間ですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Fellow rain-shelterers, then.

lines.japaneseText: 寒すぎて、知らない人とも団結できそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: It's cold enough that strangers could form an alliance.

lines.japaneseText: 二人ともすごく楽しそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You two look like you're having a great time.
lines.notes: Address both of them. Ignoring the friend is the single most common way this goes wrong.

lines.japaneseText: 二人ともおしゃれですね。方向性が違っていい感じです。
lines.englishMeaning: You're both stylish, and in different directions, which is great.

lines.japaneseText: どっちかだけに声かけるのも変なので、二人に挨拶しに来ました。
lines.englishMeaning: It would be odd to talk to just one of you, so I came to greet you both.
lines.notes: Honest and disarming. Do not then peel one of them away; build a friendly interaction with both first.

lines.japaneseText: すごく仲良さそうですね。
lines.englishMeaning: You two seem close.

lines.japaneseText: どっちが今日ここに来ようって言ったんですか？
lines.englishMeaning: Which of you suggested coming here today?
lines.followUpSuggestion: A good second question because it includes them both.

lines.japaneseText: 率直に言うと、すごくタイプです。
lines.englishMeaning: To be direct about it, you're very much my type.

lines.japaneseText: 迷ったんですけど、話しかけないほうが後悔すると思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: I hesitated, but I decided I'd regret not saying something.

lines.japaneseText: ナンパというより、普通に知り合いたいと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: This isn't really a pick-up. I just wanted to get to know you.

lines.japaneseText: いきなり連絡先じゃなくて、まず少し話したいです。
lines.englishMeaning: Rather than asking for your number straight away, I'd like to talk a little first.
lines.notes: Reassuring precisely because it asks for less than expected.

lines.japaneseText: 急にすみません。迷惑だったらすぐ行きます。すごく素敵だと思いました。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry to appear out of nowhere. I'll go if this is unwelcome. I thought you looked wonderful.
lines.notes: Hands her the exit in the same breath as the compliment. That is what makes a direct approach acceptable.

lines.japaneseText: また会えたら嬉しいです。
lines.englishMeaning: I'd be glad to see you again.
lines.notes: A gentle close that does not require an answer on the spot.

lines.japaneseText: この話、また続きしたいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: I'd like to pick this conversation up again.
lines.notes: Works when there is a genuinely unfinished topic.

lines.japaneseText: そのおすすめ、あとで送ってほしいです。
lines.englishMeaning: I'd like you to send me that recommendation later.
lines.followUpSuggestion: Gives an ordinary, practical reason to exchange contacts.

lines.japaneseText: 次はもう少しゆっくり話したいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: Next time I'd like to talk somewhere a bit calmer.

lines.japaneseText: また会いたいので、連絡できるようにしてもいいですか？
lines.englishMeaning: I'd like to see you again. Could we exchange contact details?
lines.notes: Straightforward and easy to decline, which is the point.

lines.japaneseText: 今日話せてよかったです。また連絡したいです。
lines.englishMeaning: I'm glad we talked. I'd like to stay in touch.

lines.japaneseText: インスタ交換したら、次のイベント分かりやすいですね。
lines.englishMeaning: If we swap Instagram it'll be easier to know about the next event.

lines.japaneseText: すみません、急に声かけて。よい一日を。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry for approaching out of the blue. Have a good day.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 邪魔してすみません。楽しんでください。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry to have interrupted. Enjoy your day.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: お友達との時間にすみませんでした。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry for interrupting your time with your friend.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 急いでるところ、失礼しました。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry, I can see you're in a hurry.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 大丈夫です、ありがとうございます。
lines.englishMeaning: That's completely fine, thank you.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: では、よい夜を。
lines.englishMeaning: Have a good evening, then.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 話してくれてありがとうございました。
lines.englishMeaning: Thank you for talking with me.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: ちょっとでも話せてよかったです。
lines.englishMeaning: I'm glad we got to talk, even briefly.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 仕事中にすみません。頑張ってください。
lines.englishMeaning: Sorry to interrupt you at work. Good luck with it.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.

lines.japaneseText: 気にしないでください。失礼します。
lines.englishMeaning: Please don't give it a thought. I'll leave you to it.
lines.notes: Say it once, warmly, and then actually leave. A graceful exit matters more than any opener.
